title: The Pattern That Never Breaks
label: ch:zahlen-13-20
canDo: I can count from thirteen to twenty in German and build every one of those numbers from a digit I already know.

payoff.summary: One rule run eight times: a digit you already own with zehn welded on the end, which is what English -teen is too, because -teen IS ten. Two digits are trimmed at the join -- sechs loses its s and sieben loses its -en -- and that is the mouth economising, not the rule breaking, exactly as English wore three down to thir- and five to fif-. Twenty stops using zehn and uses -zig, which is the same word worn further, and so is English -ty. The Romance sisters all break partway through the teens; German does not break at all.
payoff.note: Chapter 19 is generated from schema-v2 lessons and introduces eleven atoms, one under the ceiling. A three-way split of the old chapter (3/6/5) was considered and rejected: eleven fits, and splitting below the ceiling for its own sake is not the rule. Every teen is ASSEMBLED from a digit the reader already owns plus zehn, so the chapter is a machine being run rather than eight words being memorised.
